proposed_comments.title: Preserve legacy history when qualifying keys with an AUMID
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve legacy history when qualifying keys with an AUMID

**Severity:** `high`

This changes the persisted identity from the executable path to `<path>?<AUMID>`, but existing `app-path` records contain only the executable path and every lookup/removal below uses the new exact key. After upgrade, previously saved zones therefore stop applying to AUMID windows. A direct fallback to the legacy vector is also unsafe because removing one qualified identity can mutate history still shared by sibling AUMIDs.

Please add a helper that strips the AUMID suffix, copy legacy history into a new qualified entry before the first mutation, and clear copied runtime handle maps. Lookups may fall back to the legacy entry only while no qualified entry exists; removals must materialize the qualified copy before changing it. Preserve an explicit empty qualified entry as a tombstone during JSON load and virtual-desktop cleanup so a removed AUMID does not fall back and resurrect legacy history.

confidence.rationale: The live diff changes all four history lookups to an AUMID-qualified key without a migration path. The converged fork implements copy-on-migration, qualified tombstones, and fallback isolation, and its exact head rebuilt successfully.

proposed_comments.title: Add AUMID migration and helper regression coverage
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The required unit-test and UI-test helper files are unchanged by the live upstream PR, so GitHub has no current RIGHT-side diff range for this coverage.
proposed_comments.body:
### Add AUMID migration and helper regression coverage

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:**
- `src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesTests/UnitTests/AppZoneHistoryTests.Spec.cpp` - `AppZoneHistoryUnitTests`
- `src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZones.UITests/Utils/ZoneSwitchHelper.cs` - `GetZoneIndexSetByAppName`
- `src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZones.UITests.Next/Utils/ZoneHistory.cs` - `GetZoneIndexSetByAppName`

**Problem:** The PR changes the persisted `app-path` key format, but it does not test isolation between two AUMIDs, migration from an existing process-path-only record, persistence of an empty qualified tombstone, or UI-test lookup of an executable name when the saved key has an AUMID suffix.

**Why it matters:** Without these checks, a future edit can silently merge browser profiles, erase another profile's legacy history, resurrect a removed placement after reload, or make both FancyZones UI-test suites fail to locate otherwise valid history.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add a test helper that assigns distinct `PKEY_AppUserModel_ID` values to test windows.
2. Verify two windows from the same executable keep independent zone histories.
3. Seed a legacy executable-path entry, access it through a qualified window, mutate the qualified entry, and assert the legacy entry remains unchanged.
4. Remove the qualified history, reload and synchronize virtual desktops, and assert the empty qualified tombstone remains while legacy history is still available to unqualified windows.
5. In both UI-test helpers, strip the substring beginning at `?` before applying the executable-name suffix comparison.

**Verification:** Build `src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesTests/UnitTests/UnitTests.vcxproj` and both FancyZones UI-test projects. Run the focused AUMID history tests and confirm both helper implementations find entries whose saved `app-path` is `<executable>?<AUMID>`.

confidence.rationale: These exact out-of-diff tests and helper changes exist in the converged fork. The unit-test project builds, while the local native test host still exits with 0xC0000005 before reporting individual tests, matching the previously documented environment blocker.

test_instructions: Enable FancyZones and zone two windows from the same browser executable that use different taskbar identities, then confirm each identity restores its own zone.
Start with a legacy process-path-only history file, zone one qualified window, and confirm the legacy placement still applies to an unqualified window.
Remove the qualified placement, restart PowerToys, and confirm that identity remains unzoned instead of falling back to the legacy placement.
